clue.text: Star part chosen by Bassanio?

definitions.meaning: the principal role in a play or film
in The Merchant of Venice Bassanio wins Portia by picking the casket made of this metal

explanation.surface: A question about which role a Shakespearean character would pick.
explanation.definitionFit: The starring role is the leading one, and Bassanio's winning casket was the plain grey metal one.

clue.text: Green plants of doctor on board

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
SS, steamship, as in 'on board SS so-and-so'

explanation.surface: Plants seen on the deck of a ship where a doctor serves.
explanation.definitionFit: Mosses are small green non-flowering plants.

clue.text: Advantage of golf-club going topless?

indicators.note: losing the top, i.e. the first letter of the club's name, in a down clue

parts.note: a wedge is a lofted golf club

explanation.surface: A golfer's edge from a club with its head knocked off.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge over a rival is an advantage.

clue.text: Stroke, perhaps, of one in eight

definitions.meaning: the stroke is the rower setting the pace in a boat
a member of an eight, a rowing crew

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a stroke befalls one person in eight.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower may be the stroke, and a racing eight has eight rowers.

clue.text: Pretence of showing up?

definitions.meaning: a false show, keeping up a front

explanation.surface: Asking whether turning up is mere show.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping up a facade is a pretence, and arriving somewhere is making yourself seen there.

clue.text: Doesn't care about what is mediocre

indicators.note: about signals the letters being turned around and reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone indifferent to anything merely average.
explanation.definitionFit: Something second-class and inferior is mediocre.

clue.text: Derivation of English mother-race

parts.note: MA is mother
a race or people can be a nation

explanation.surface: Tracing the ancestry of an English mother's people.
explanation.definitionFit: Something issuing from a source, an outflow or derivative.

clue.text: Ceremonial cloak for work in church

definitions.text: Ceremonial cloak for work in church

parts.words: Ceremonial cloak for work in church
parts.note: a long semicircular vestment worn by clergy at services and processions

explanation.definitionFit: The cope is a liturgical vestment worn by priests.

clue.text: Dry places ruined this old timer…

indicators.note: ruined says the letters are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Arid spots that wrecked an ancient device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old timer' suggests a veteran, but here it is a water clock used in antiquity.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient water clock, measuring time by dripping water.

clue.text: Post-prandial discomfort, said Pepys, suffering

indicators.note: suffering puts the words into distress, rearranging them

explanation.surface: The diarist reporting indigestion after dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigestion after a meal.

clue.text: … old character needing hip replacement

indicators.note: a replacement here rearranges the three letters of the joint

explanation.surface: An elderly person awaiting hip surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek letter, a character of an ancient alphabet.

clue.text: Plane from Stevenage?

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the town's name

explanation.surface: A flight leaving a Hertfordshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane surface is flat and level.

clue.text: Pinch a dram

definitions.meaning: a sharp squeeze between finger and thumb

explanation.surface: Stealing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A nip is both a small squeeze and a small tot of whisky.

clue.text: Grass in which Spanish girl embraces boy?

indicators.note: embraces means the girl's name goes around the boy's

parts.note: Maria is a Spanish girl's name
Juan is a Spanish boy's name

explanation.surface: A romantic scene on a lawn between a Spanish girl and a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass is slang for cannabis.

clue.text: Tails necessary for this formal wear?

definitions.text: Tails necessary for this formal wear?

parts.words: Tails necessary for this formal wear?
parts.note: tails are a tailcoat, but also what a primate has, so formal evening dress jokingly needs a primate's tail

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a dress suit or tuxedo.

clue.text: Like Gershwin piece I do badly in C sharp perhaps

indicators.note: in places the reworked pair of words inside the other rearrangement
perhaps says the musical key's letters may come out in another order
badly means the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A musician confessing to playing poorly in a sharp key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' makes ODI from I DO, and 'perhaps' makes RHAPSC from C SHARP; ODI goes in before the final C.
explanation.definitionFit: Gershwin's Rhapsody in Blue is a rhapsody, so in that style.

clue.text: Unauthorised departure from Reading maybe?

parts.note: Reading, the English town, has a famous gaol, so leaving it without permission is an escape

explanation.walkthrough: Reading Gaol, made famous by Oscar Wilde, is the prison in the English town of Reading; 'Reading' at the start of a clue hides its capital.
explanation.definitionFit: An escape from a prison.

clue.text: Generator is returned to engineers

indicators.note: returned means the little word is read backwards

parts.note: RE stands for Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: A power unit being sent back to the engineering corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A father, one who begets, generates offspring.

clue.text: Circular letters about train wrecked in Canada

indicators.note: about means the round letters surround the rest

parts.note: O is a round letter, and two of them

indicators.note: wrecked says the train's letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A train crash in Canada reported in round-robin letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A province of the country.

clue.text: Mandatory book-fastening?

definitions.meaning: the cover that holds a book's pages together

explanation.surface: Asking whether a book's cover is compulsory.
explanation.definitionFit: A binding agreement is obligatory, and a book's binding holds its pages.

clue.text: Battle in which mother caught spy

indicators.note: caught means the mother word holds the other inside

parts.note: MA is mother
a spy is an agent

explanation.surface: A war story where a mother captures a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1859 Battle of Magenta, in Italy, gave its name to the dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta was an 1859 battle of the Second Italian War of Independence.

clue.text: Twit, we hear, in river

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is said aloud

parts.note: to twit is to tease

explanation.surface: A fool in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tees is a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A river of north-east England.

clue.text: Inspiration to win a scrap in courageous style?

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged words within the bold word

parts.note: courageous means brave

indicators.note: to scrap something breaks it up, here the letters

explanation.surface: Winning a fight with bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden clever idea.

clue.text: Raillery from comedian

explanation.surface: Banter coming from a stand-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Humour is banter, and a witty person is a joker.

clue.text: Port's finished with Old English, right?

parts.note: R is right

explanation.surface: A poet concluding with an archaic tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Poets contract 'over' to o'er, and over means finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Over, meaning ended, contracted in verse.

clue.text: Employ in university, but in classics

parts.note: U is university
sed is Latin for but

explanation.surface: Taking a job at a college teaching Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: 'employ' must be read as 'employed', the past form.
explanation.definitionFit: Employed is put to use.

clue.text: Muscles needed for lifts

definitions.meaning: muscles that raise a part of the body
American word for lifts in buildings

explanation.surface: Body-building muscles needed for lifting weights.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising muscles are so named, and American lifts carry people between floors.

clue.text: Laws can be boring things

indicators.note: can be says the word may be rearranged into another

explanation.surface: A complaint that legislation is dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointed tools for piercing holes.

clue.text: Likelihood of loose sod about end of round

indicators.note: about means the jumbled turf goes around the final letter
loose says the turf's letters are rearranged
end of picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A loose clod around the end of a golf round.
explanation.definitionFit: Chances or probability.

clue.text: Weapons put up in bar of pub?

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: guns are weapons

explanation.surface: Arms displayed in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A snug is a small private bar in a British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosy small room in a British pub.

clue.text: Record field-event leaving America behind…

indicators.note: leaving says one word is dropped from the other
behind completes the idea of the country's letters left off

parts.note: the discus is a field event
US is America

explanation.surface: An athlete setting a record abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record.

clue.text: … one stands on platform, under pressure, waiting to be beaten

definitions.text: one stands on platform, under pressure, waiting to be beaten

parts.words: one stands on platform, under pressure, waiting to be beaten
parts.note: sounds like a nervous person awaiting defeat, but an orchestra's percussion instrument stands on a stage and is struck

explanation.definitionFit: A timpano, a large drum played with sticks in an orchestra.
